input.rubric_description: Shows the judgement expected at the target role level.

excerpts.text: In the October session on incident response, I described the first thirty minutes of a payment outage and the decisions I made before the incident bridge opened. I named the service, the four dependent teams and the weekly release volume, then explained the staged cutover, the tested rollback and the point where I stopped the change. The answer covered the customer impact, the person who owned the final decision and the evidence I used to show that the new sequence reduced lead time from nine days to four. I described the trade-off between speed and safety, the escalation I chose when the error rate crossed the threshold, and the review I wrote the following morning. The follow-up question was about the person who disagreed with the plan, and I answered with the specific conversation, the concession I made and the point I held. The practice report recorded the same gap in two places, so the excerpt is long enough to show how the answer actually sounded.

In the July session on commercial judgement, I set out how I reduced cloud spend without moving the reliability target. I described the trade-off between speed and safety, the escalation I chose when the error rate crossed the threshold, and the review I wrote the following morning. I said what I personally owned, what the platform team owned and how I checked that the saving did not depend on removing a control the auditors expected. The result included the change in first-time fix rate, the two releases that needed no rollback and the feedback from the shift managers who used the new checklist. I ended with the evidence I would bring to a panel: the before-and-after measure, the review document and the name of the person who signed off the change. The practice report recorded the same gap in two places, so the excerpt is long enough to show how the answer actually sounded.
